right_or_protection_name: Right to seek information from central public authorities (online filing)
plain_language_explanation: Indian citizens can ask central government bodies for information they hold. For central bodies this can be done online through the RTI Online portal, which gives a registration number to track the request.
legal_basis: Right to Information Act, 2005 (Act 22 of 2005). The portal FAQ refers to section 6(3) for transfer of misdirected applications. Other section numbers not verified here.
who_may_be_eligible: Indian citizens (per the portal). Applicants below the poverty line are exempt from the fee under the RTI Rules, 2012, per the portal FAQ.
conditions_and_exceptions: Portal is only for central ministries, departments and public authorities. Applications for state public authorities, including NCT of Delhi, are returned without refund. Text box limit is 3000 characters; longer text can be uploaded as a PDF. BPL applicants must attach their certificate. Exemptions to disclosure in the Act were not reviewed.
how_to_exercise_or_access: Use Submit Request on rtionline.gov.in, choose the public authority, enter the request text, pay the prescribed fee (net banking, card or UPI) unless BPL, and note the registration number. Track via View Status (OTP-protected).
complaint_or_application_process: Request goes to the authority's Nodal Officer who forwards it to the CPIO. Additional fee, if any, is notified through View Status.
responsible_authority: Central Public Information Officer of the relevant authority; portal run by DoPT

plain_language_explanation: If you are unhappy with, or get no reply to, an RTI request to a central authority, you can file a first appeal. No fee is charged.
legal_basis: Right to Information Act, 2005 (first appeal provision; section number not verified here).
who_may_be_eligible: Applicants whose RTI request was filed online with the portal.
conditions_and_exceptions: Per the portal FAQ: online first appeal is possible only against an RTI filed online; if there has been no reply, appeal only after 30 days; if the request was physically transferred to a non-aligned authority the appeal must be filed physically. Statutory appeal time limits were not verified.
how_to_exercise_or_access: Choose Submit First Appeal on rtionline.gov.in and enter the registration number and email ID of the original request.
complaint_or_application_process: Second appeal or complaint to the Central Information Commission; the CIC portal is integrated and can pull details from the RTI Online record.
responsible_authority: First Appellate Authority of the public authority; Central Information Commission for second appeal

right_or_protection_name: Free legal services under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
plain_language_explanation: People who fall in certain listed groups, or whose income is below a limit, can get a lawyer and other legal help free through legal services authorities. It is not available to everyone.
legal_basis: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987: Section 12 (who is entitled), Section 13 (entitlement requires satisfying the authority that there is a genuine case to prosecute or defend), Section 2(c) (meaning of legal services).
who_may_be_eligible: Section 12 categories as shown on the Kerala SLSA page: SC/ST members; victims of trafficking or begar; women and children; persons with disabilities; persons in undeserved want after a mass disaster, violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster; industrial workmen; persons in custody (including protective, juvenile or psychiatric facilities); and persons under an annual income ceiling (that page shows Rs 3 lakh, or more if the state prescribes, for courts other than the Supreme Court, and a higher figure for the Supreme Court, but the text was cut off).
conditions_and_exceptions: Must satisfy the authority that there is a genuine case (Section 13(1)). Senior citizen eligibility depends on state rules (per a NALSA subdomain page). Income ceilings can be raised by states. List and amounts must be confirmed against the current Act.
how_to_exercise_or_access: Apply to NALSA or the State/District Legal Services Authority, including via the NALSA online portal, at any stage of a case if eligible.
complaint_or_application_process: Application to the concerned Legal Services Authority; for Karnataka, the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (not yet collected).
responsible_authority: NALSA; State and District Legal Services Authorities

right_or_protection_name: Reporting online financial fraud via 1930 and the national cybercrime portal
plain_language_explanation: If you lose money to an online scam, you can call the national helpline 1930 and file a complaint on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal. Reporting quickly helps investigators act before evidence disappears.
legal_basis: Not established here. This is a reporting mechanism, and no statutory right or section was verified.
who_may_be_eligible: Victims of cybercrime, including online financial fraud.
conditions_and_exceptions: The portal handles cybercrime complaints only. Speed matters but no deadline was verified from an official source.
how_to_exercise_or_access: Call 1930 (stated as available 24 hours a day by the Kerala Police notice) and file a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
complaint_or_application_process: Complaint on the portal; progress can be tracked there per the police notice.
responsible_authority: Ministry of Home Affairs / I4C; state police for investigation
